newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares rise on ADR plans, seen up.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares rise on ADR plans, seen up.

text.p: Most leading Russian shares forged ahead in early trade on Friday and traders, though cautious, said the market could close up several points.
The Russian Trading System 22-share index opened slightly up at 357.38 after closing on Thursday at 357.00.
"It's not all one way -- I wouldn't say the whole market is going up, just some blue chips. I think the market will be up a couple of percent today," said Rinaco-Plus trader Tom Brackenbury.

Norilsk Nickel continued to sizzle after gaining about six percent on Thursday, rising at 0915 GMT to $7.08 at from $6.35 at Thursday's close on company plans to issue American Depositary Receipts by July, traders said.
National power company UES rose to $0.3175 at from $0.3037 on Thursday. Irkutskenergo edged up to $0.294 from $0.286.
"I haven't heard Dow Jones mentioned in past few days," Brackenbury said, saying the morning rise was on Western demand and plans by some leading companies to issue ADRs in the near future.

Peter Kizenko, chief equities trader at ING Barings said the RTS index could touch its Monday record of 360.72, but other traders were more cautious, seeing Western investors setting the pace later in the day.
"There is some demand from Western investors but it's not new money," said Rossiisky Kredit Bank trader Oleg Martynenko.
"It depends on American investors -- when New York opens they'll say what they think about this market, whether they'll buy or not."
And Rinaco Plus's Brackenbury said the market did not seem to be taking into account significant political events next week.
The Russian State Duma, the lower house of parliament, is due to debate budget cuts proposed by the government next week, as well as a proposal that the govenment authorise new issues of cash.
"I guess maybe we should be a little more concerned about the budget debate next week...but no-one seems to be taking the slightest bit of notice of it," he said.
